rules.title: Annual General Adjustment (AGA) capped at 5%
rules.quote: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.summary: The Annual General Adjustment, which is the maximum amount landlords of fully-covered rental units may raise rent each year, is capped at 5%.
rules.exemption_note: Units where tenant shares kitchen or bath with landlord are exempt only if landlord lived there before tenant moved in; new construction units (certificate of occupancy after 1980), most single-family homes, and most condominiums are partially covered only

rules.title: Nonpayment eviction requires rental debt of at least one month Fair Market Rent
rules.quote: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.summary: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent unless the tenant owes at least one month of the HUD Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size in the Oakland-Fremont metro area.
rules.coverage_text: applies to tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.exemption_note: Units where tenant shares kitchen or bath with landlord who lived there first are exempt; applies to fully or partially covered units

rules.title: Prohibition on eviction for failure to sign new lease
rules.quote: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot evict tenants for refusing to sign a new lease that is substantially similar to their previous lease when the fixed-term lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: applies to tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.exemption_note: applies to fully or partially covered units

rules.title: New requirements for eviction based on lease violations
rules.quote: The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant's behavior was unreasonable. The landlord's notice to the tenant to stop the violation (which is required before the landlord can serve an eviction notice) must specify the lease term, and describe the violation and resulting harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.
rules.summary: To evict a tenant for violating a material lease term, the landlord must show the violation caused substantial actual damage, the tenant's behavior was unreasonable, and the notice must clearly describe the lease term, violation, and harm.
rules.coverage_text: applies to tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.exemption_note: applies to fully or partially covered units

rules.title: Eviction notice content and filing requirements
rules.quote: Any notice terminating a tenancy must contain a statement that advice about the notice is available from the Rent Board, the current phone number for the Rent Board's Housing counseling services, and the current address of the Rent Board's website. The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.
rules.summary: Eviction notices must include Rent Board contact information and advice availability, and landlords must file copies of eviction notices and lawsuits with the Rent Board within three business days of serving the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: applies to any notice terminating a tenancy

rules.title: Annual adjustment of owner move-in eviction relocation assistance
rules.quote: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments to owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts each year.
rules.summary: The Rent Board is required to annually adjust the relocation assistance amounts that landlords must pay to tenants evicted for owner move-in based on inflation.
